chunk_findings.detail: The regression test does not actually prove that the baseline gate was run at the fork. The injected `run` callback is not recorded, and the assertions only inspect the final `outcome` and the `ev["baseline"]` dictionary. An implementation that computes `_branch_base` correctly for display but skips the baseline execution (or runs it in an unrelated directory that happens to contain a `healthy` file) and hard-codes `ev["baseline"] = {"red": False, "base_sha": fork}` would pass all assertions in this fixture. In a real repository where the fork itself is red, that implementation would incorrectly report `red=False` and would not treat the failure as baseline-red. The test should capture the baseline invocation’s `where`/gate (for example, by recording calls and asserting the baseline `where` is a checkout whose `git rev-parse HEAD` is `fork`) rather than only checking the reported baseline result.

data.body: ddflow next prints the INTERRUPTED / running / blocked / merged-not-completed COUNTS but has no flag to LIST items by state. Scripts and lanes grep the text ("INTERRUPTED:") to enumerate them. Add `ddflow next --state <interrupted|running|blocked|ready|merged|...>` (and echo it in --json) so a lane can get exactly the running or interrupted set machine-readably instead of grepping. Lists per-state, carries the same paging/--full/--json caps, CLI + MCP parity for the ddflow_next tool. Tests first.
data.title: ddflow next --state: list interrupted/running/blocked items, not just counts
